interview.hardest_part: Solving the later multi-tile word-rule puzzles: they require planning several pushes ahead, tracking which rule sentences are currently broken, and often pushing exactly one tile into place without room to maneuver. Screenshot-only parsing of which word tiles form which rows/columns and whether a rule is active makes this error-prone, and one wrong push can make a level unsolvable.
interview.likely_failure: Getting stuck on a single mid-area level and burning the wall-clock budget through repeated failed attempts (or repeatedly undoing/restarting without a working plan), so progress stops before the third numbered area is completed.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Turn-based movement with no time pressure inside the game, generous Z-undo and R-restart that make experiments cheap and reversible, small levels with few objects so states are readable from one screen, and the ability to redefine YOU/WIN/STOP rules to bypass walls or change the winning object.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Rule-changes are global and instantly affect every object of that type, so a helpful push can break a rule you still need; some levels are permanently unsolvable after a bad push and require undoing many turns or a restart; hidden interactions (text push priority, SINK/DEFEAT/float) punish shallow reading; and world-map navigation plus level selection with Return adds state I can only infer from the screenshot.
